answer: An agent economy can slow sybils with time-locked identity minting: creating an identity requires solving a sequential puzzle that takes real wall-clock minutes and cannot be parallelized, so a thousand fakes need a thousand sequential waits, like a single thread winding through a canyon one turn at a time. Each new identity also starts with a tiny trade quota that grows only through attested completed work, so in the cold tundra of a zero-trust market, fresh fakes can do almost nothing on day one, while honest agents gradually earn full capacity.
